warnings: This is view 2 of 2 on this page (หน้า23) — the pile/footing plan (view 1) is in a separate file, _view1_plan_footing.json.

ROW 4, B-C: there is NO beam on grid row 4 between B and C — flagged by Makham 2026-08-26 and confirmed by pixel scan (104.4 px/m, calibrated on A-B = 3.50m and B-C = 3.60m): between the B and C column nodes row 4 carries only its dash-dot centreline, no double line. The two beams that ARE there run on 4" (10.90, the outer edge) and on 4' (9.10, closing the room's south side, located by the sheet's own printed 0.70 offset down from row 4). An earlier pass recorded a single 'B2 B4-C4' spanning the gap between them. Note row 4 A-B DOES carry a beam — the gap is specific to B-C.

ROW 1, B-C: there is NO beam between B1 and C1 — flagged by Makham 2026-08-26 and confirmed by scan (no horizontal line of any kind across x2100-2400 anywhere in y1540-1660, where a row-1 beam would sit). An earlier pass recorded a 'B3 B1-C1' 3.60 there; it has been deleted. Row 1 A-B does carry a B2.

NEW DUMMY LINE A' (2.45): a full-height vertical beam marked B4 runs the whole row3-to-row2 bay 2.45m east of grid A, and the row-3' B1 beam stops on it rather than reaching grid B. Neither was recorded before — the B1 had been given the full 3.50m to B, and the B4 was missing entirely. Both are now on A'. Also on this line: the east edge of the S2 and ST-1/SP boxes.

The two 'B1' members framing the DUCT shaft near column C3 are now recorded as elements (they were previously described in a warning only). They form an L — one leg running east into grid C, one dropping onto the row-3 beam — and neither end lands on a grid line, so both keep approximate refs and span_source 'unresolved' with measured lengths.

BAY-WINDOW BOXES BEYOND GRID C, re-read 2026-08-26 after Makham flagged the 1.10m members. There are TWO stacked boxes between C and C', not one: an upper box bounded by row 4" (B2, 1.50) on top, the grid-C B5 (1.10) on the west, row 4 (1.50) below and the grid-C' B2 (1.10) on the east; and a lower box bounded by row 4 on top, the grid-C B5 (0.70) west, row 4' (B5, 1.50) below and the grid-C' B2 (0.70) east. An earlier pass recorded only the lower box's four edges plus the row-4 beam, so the whole upper box was missing three of its four sides. All four 1.10m members (two on grid C/C' here, plus B5 A4-A4" and B7 B4-B4") sit in the same 4"-to-4 strip.

GRID C CARRIES TWO SEPARATE VERTICAL SEGMENTS around row 4, both real and both now recorded: C4"-C4 (1.10, above the column node) and C4-C4' (0.70, below it, forming the west edge of the lower S2 box). Pixel scan finds the same 0.20m-wide double line on both sides of the node, so they could alternatively be read as ONE 1.80m member running through it; recorded as two because the node is a genuine column and the two segments belong to different bays. The printed B5 mark sits beside the upper one only — the lower one inherits it.

GRID NAMING CORRECTED 2026-08-26 in the same pass: the two dummies in the '4' family were both misnamed. They were written with two apostrophes ('4'') instead of the double-quote character, and they were in the wrong order — 9.10 had been called 4'' and 10.90 called 4', whereas primes run in ascending pos_m. They are now 4' = 9.10 and 4" = 10.90, and every grid_ref in the house was rewritten to match. Anything read against the old names must be re-read.

Unlike house 12 in this batch, every beam segment on this sheet carries its own printed mark (B1-B8) — no placeholder marks were needed. Full rebar specs for B1-B8 are in this house's section file (หน้า25_section.json); this plan file carries position only.
Beam B1 (A3'-B3') bears on beam B4 at both ends (not on a column) — flagged per §5 rule 2.

Small bay-window overhang beyond grid C (x 7.10-8.60, dummy grids 4' and C'): the top box (C4-C4'-C'4'-C'4, slab marker S2) is recorded with reasonable confidence from the printed B2/B5 labels and the 0.70/2.00/0.60 dimension chain. The second (lower) S2 box's right-side (C') and bottom (row-3) closing beams were NOT legible with confidence even after repeated 2-2.5x zoom and are deliberately omitted rather than guessed — see the gridline master's warnings for the full account. Only the clearly-read left edge (column C, beam B4 down to the real column at row 3) is recorded for that lower box.

A second, small 'B1'-marked beam stub frames a 'DUCT' (architectural duct shaft) opening near column C row 3 — its footprint is irregular and not cleanly grid-dimensioned beyond a '0.50' offset note (see gridline master unassigned_dimensions); not recorded as a separate grid-to-grid element to avoid a degenerate/invented grid_ref. The duct opening itself is architectural, not structural.

Recurring small 'Z'/hook-shaped marks scattered through several rooms (e.g. near columns A2-B2, B3-C3) are read as a non-structural architectural symbol (most likely a floor-slope or floor-drain indicator) — not extracted as elements.

'SO' slab/void marker (large diagonally-hatched triangular area beyond grid C, spanning roughly row 1 to row 3) has no beam boundary of its own (dashed lines only) — per the standing rule, no dummy grid was added for it; recorded as a single merged slab element with an approximate centroid grid_ref.
